name: Cinnamon Bark (True/Ceylon)
source_reference: ISO 3524:2004 - Oil of cinnamon bark; Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960; Jayaprakasha et al., J. Agric. Food Chem., 2003
notes: True cinnamon bark oil is distinct from cassia (C. cassia) which has higher cinnamaldehyde (>80%) and significant coumarin. Ceylon cinnamon bark oil has notable eugenol content. Cinnamon leaf oil is eugenol-dominant (70-80%).

key_markers.14371-10-9: trans-Cinnamaldehyde - defines the hot, sweet, spicy cinnamon character
key_markers.97-53-0: Eugenol - clove-spicy warmth, distinguishes Ceylon from cassia
key_markers.103-54-8: Cinnamyl acetate - sweet balsamic ester, quality marker for true cinnamon

olfactive_description: Warm, sweet, intensely spicy with a distinctive hot, dry character. Rich balsamic-woody undertones with a soft clove-like eugenol warmth. More refined and complex than cassia.
